title: Baked Stuffed Apples
subtitle: Oat and honey filled baked apples
excerpt: Large apples cored and filled with a mixture of oats, honey, butter, and cinnamon, then baked until soft and golden. Simple enough for a weeknight but good enough to serve to guests.
sourceNotes: Based on the traditional British baked apple, a reliable autumn and winter pudding that needs very little preparation.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare and fill the apples up to 4 hours ahead, then bake when needed.

content.text: Score the skin around the middle of each apple before baking. This stops them from bursting as they soften in the oven.
Core the apples using an apple corer or a small sharp knife. Widen the cavity a little to hold plenty of filling.
Score the skin around the middle of each apple with a knife.
Mix the oats, honey, butter pieces, cinnamon, almonds, and nutmeg in a small bowl.
Place the apples in a roasting tin. Pack the oat mixture firmly into each cavity.
Add 4 tbsp of water to the bottom of the tin. Bake for 30 minutes until the apples are soft throughout.
Serve warm with any syrupy juices from the tin spooned over.

items.symptom: Apples burst and collapsed in the oven.
items.cause: Skin was not scored before baking.
items.fix: Score the equator of each apple next time before filling.

items.symptom: Filling has dried out and gone hard.
items.cause: No liquid in the tin and oven too hot.
items.fix: Add water to the tin and cover loosely with foil halfway through.

items.symptom: Apple is still firm after 30 minutes.
items.cause: Very large or hard variety of apple.
items.fix: Return to the oven for 10 more minutes and check with a knife.
